findings: An infiltrative pancreatic cancer measuring 57 mm is observed in the tail of the pancreas. Serosal invasion and retropancreatic tissue invasion are noted. There is contact of more than 180° with the superior mesenteric vein, suggesting invasion. No invasion beyond the inferior border of the duodenum is observed. Prominent soft tissue shadows around the vessels raise suspicion of extrapancreatic nerve plexus invasion. No other local invasion factors are identified. Lymph node metastases are observed in three nodes at station 14t and one node at station 18. Multiple liver metastases are observed.

responses.content:
Task 1: Diagnose the local invasion factors of pancreatic cancer.

CH0 (no invasion of the common hepatic artery)
DU0 (no invasion beyond the inferior border of the duodenum)
S1 (serosal invasion)
RP1 (extrapancreatic nerve plexus invasion)
PV0 (no invasion of the portal vein)
A0 (no invasion of the abdominal aorta)
PL0 (no invasion of the pancreatic lymphatic vessels)
OO1 (retropancreatic tissue invasion)

Task 2: Determine the classification for local invasion (T classification) of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the size of the tumor (57 mm) and the presence of serosal invasion, retropancreatic tissue invasion, and contact with the superior mesenteric vein, the T classification is T3.

Task 3: Determine the N classification of pancreatic cancer.

Regional lymph nodes for pancreatic cancer in the tail are:
- Station 14t (left gastric artery lymph nodes)
- Station 17 (common hepatic artery lymph nodes)
- Station 18 (splenic artery lymph nodes)
- Station 14d (left gastric artery lymph nodes)
- Station 13 (suprapyloric lymph nodes)
- Station 16 (common hepatic artery lymph nodes)

Metastatic lymph nodes are observed in stations 14t and 18, which are regional lymph nodes. Counting only the metastatic lymph nodes within the regional stations, there are 4 involved regional nodes. Therefore, the N classification is N1b.

Task 4: Determine the M classification of pancreatic cancer.

Multiple liver metastases are observed, indicating distant metastases. Therefore, the M classification is M1.

Task 5: Determine the resectability classification of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the presence of distant metastases (M1), the tumor is classified as Unresectable (UR).

Task 6: Determine the overall stage according to the JPS staging system.

Based on the T classification (T3), N classification (N1b), and M classification (M1), the overall stage is Stage IV.
